items_missed: Never asked the customer's name — she volunteered it near the end ('I'm Josi by the way') and he still never used it once, not even in the farewell.
No 'how are you today?' and no agenda statement at all — went straight from 'how can I help you' into intake questions, so the customer never knew the shape or length of the call.

Never stated the hourly rate, the number of movers, or the per-mover-per-hour structure. Quoted a bare '$485 starting price,' which caused two rounds of confusion — the customer asked 'is it 485 for the first hour?' and had to be corrected.

Clock mechanics half-explained: gave the 2.5 hour minimum but never said the clock starts on-site at contract open, never mentioned 15-minute prorated increments, and never sense-checked with 'does that make sense?' despite audible confusion.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — 'insurance' appeared only as one word inside the included-items list, with no $2,000 figure and no 60c/lb baseline contrast.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — he described the 8:30-9:00 AM and 12:30-2:30 PM windows in detail, which was the natural opening for the discount-immediately promise, and skipped it.

Missed the 'no hidden fees' pitch on a served-up plate: the customer asked directly 'do you charge for gas or mileage... is there any other cost?' and got only 'it's just that hourly' instead of the full no-credit-card-fee / no-transportation-fee / no-fuel-surcharge / no-assembly-fee pitch.
No typical time range for the job and no mover/truck count — the customer had no way to translate $485 into an expected total.
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech absent, on a call where the customer volunteered she was 'short on man power' and the load is small enough that a carload or two would measurably cut the clock.
No booking attempt. The customer said 'I'm definitely gonna go this route' and he responded with hours instead of asking to lock in a date — the clearest buying signal in the call went unclosed.
No confirmation email mentioned, so no bolded detail list, no 'reply with any corrections,' and no 'any other questions before I let you go?'

Probe gaps on an apartment pickup: never asked about parking, elevator, walk distance, narrow hallways, HOA/COI requirements, or stairs at the destination home — all of which drive the clock he was quoting.
Never asked whether anything about the move worried her.
Fumbled the disassembly answer initially — the customer read his hesitation as a no ('no, we don't, you don't provide that') before he recovered and confirmed it is included.
top_strength: Genuine, unhurried patience under dead air. When the customer spent roughly four exchanges hunting for the destination zip code, he answered with 'Take your time' and then 'No rush at all' rather than filling the silence or pushing — that is the single warmest stretch of the call and it visibly relaxed her. He also handled the included-items list cleanly and from memory once he got to it: 'gas truck taxes, insurance, moving blanket, stretch wrap, dollies and fully equipped for any disassemble and reassembly,' plus a crisp, confident 'Not at all. We only take payment at the end of your move' on the deposit question. The no-deposit answer was the best-delivered moment in the call.
coaching_note: Zach, the highest-leverage fix is the close. This customer told you she was buying — 'I'm definitely gonna go this route, I think, instead of trying to move it ourselves' — and you answered with your office hours. That is a booked job you handed back. The line is: 'Josi, I've got Monday morning open with the guaranteed 8:30 to 9:00 arrival. There's no deposit, so let's pencil you in right now and if your neighbor's schedule shifts you just call me and we'll move it — nothing to lose.' Second priority: quote the rate, not the total. '$485 starting price' with no hourly rate, no mover count, and no 15-minute increment explanation is why she asked you the same pricing question three different ways. Say 'It's two movers at $X per hour, two and a half hour minimum, and after that we bill in 15-minute increments so you only pay for the time you actually use — does that make sense?' Third, you left all three differentiators on the table. She asked you point-blank about hidden costs and you gave her one sentence; that was the moment for the full no-hidden-fees pitch plus No Worries coverage up to $2,000, and your window explanation was the moment for the On-Time Guarantee. Finally, get her name in the first thirty seconds and use it — she had to introduce herself to you eight minutes in.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and genuinely patient during the customer's long zip-code search, and she ended the call upbeat ('fabulous, thank you again'), but the warmth stayed transactional — zero name use, no empathy markers, and 'Yes ma'am' used as reflexive filler that a couple of times answered a compound question with nothing at all.
